name: Boswellia serrata

lead: Boswellia serrata is a tree native to India whose resin (Indian frankincense) contains boswellic acids. Extracts are sold as joint and anti-inflammatory supplements, often alongside curcumin.

Its main evidence base is osteoarthritis symptoms, where meta-analyses report modest improvements in pain and function, though trials are small and often industry-linked. Relevance to appearance is indirect, via training recovery and joint comfort.

paras: Boswellic acids, especially acetyl-keto-beta-boswellic acid, inhibit 5-lipoxygenase and reduce leukotriene production, and may suppress some inflammatory cytokines.

Generally mild adverse effects such as stomach upset or diarrhea. Product standardization varies, and safety in pregnancy is not established. Legal as a dietary supplement; over-harvesting of wild trees is an ecological concern.
